Layer 1 (FILES) Belgium’s forward #09 Romelu Lukaku celebrates after scoring his team third goal during the UEFA Nations League, League A – Group 1, football match between Belgium and Turkey at the Maurice Dufrasne stadium, in Liege, eastern Belgium on October 2, 2026. Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku announced on November 16, 2026 he was retiring from international football after scoring 94 goals in 135 games for his country. “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment,” the 33-year-old said on Instagram. (Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP)
Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, bringing his 16-year Belgium career to a close as the country’s all-time leading men’s goalscorer.
The 33-year-old striker scored 94 goals in 135 appearances for the Red Devils. He made his international debut in 2010 and represented Belgium at four World Cups and three European Championships.
In a statement on social media, Lukaku said: “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. I went through every emotion possible. I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for.
“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment.”
He added: “To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.
“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable I’m grateful. Thank you.”
Lukaku is the fifth-highest men’s international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, who leads the list with 146 goals.
He scored eight goals across four World Cups, including during Belgium’s run to the quarter-finals at this summer’s tournament, and six goals at three European Championships.
In 2023, he scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, setting a record for goals in a single European Championship qualifying campaign.
